MAJOR: [OUT_OF_SCOPE] `Put` implementation still buffers the entire object into memory via `io.ReadAll` or `make([]byte, size)` (lines 218-241), violating the "True Streaming Delivery" requirement in `docs/GDRIVE-ADAPTER.md` and creating OOM risk for large files.

`retireSuperseded` and `Delete` (lines 323, 448) use `defer resp.Body.Close()` inside a loop, which can lead to file descriptor exhaustion when processing many files; bodies must be closed immediately after use.
MINOR: `findActiveFile` (line 197) and `retireSuperseded` (line 310) hardcode `pageSize=10` and `pageSize=50` respectively; if a key has more active versions than the page size, the adapter may fail to find the latest or fail to clean up all old versions.

`Put` uses `time.Now().UnixNano()` for the multipart boundary (line 249); while improved, standard practice suggests using a cryptographically random string to prevent boundary collisions with binary payloads.
NIT: `boundKey` (line 164) uses a hardcoded prefix length of 83; while safe for the 124-byte limit, it lacks a constant definition explaining the derivation (124 - 1 (separator) - 16 (hash) - 24 (buffer)).
`fileToObjectInfo` (line 595) attempts to parse `f.Size` without checking the error; while Drive API usually returns valid integers, `strconv.ParseInt` error should be handled or logged.
SUMMARY: The adapter successfully implements the `datastore.ObjectStore` interface and satisfies the permanent delete requirement.
Top risks include OOM on large uploads due to memory buffering and potential file descriptor leaks in batch deletion loops.
